questions.stem: What is the wind range for a gale warning?
questions.explanation: Strong wind 20 to 33, gale 34 to 47, storm 48 to 63, hurricane force 64 or more.

questions.stem: A forecast says 'wind northwest 25, gusts to 40'. Is a gale warning needed for that wind?
options: Yes, because the gust is over 34 knots
Yes, because 25 plus 40 is well over 34 knots
No; warnings use the mean wind and exclude gusts

questions.stem: A hurricane force wind warning means:
options: a hurricane is certain to arrive
a tropical storm is forecast for the area
wind of 64 knots or more, not a hurricane
only a gust of that strength is forecast
questions.explanation: ECCC states a hurricane force warning refers to wind speed only.

questions.stem: When and where are strong wind warnings issued on the Pacific coast?
options: All year, for the offshore areas
March 20 to Remembrance Day, for six named inner waters
December to February only, in Hecate Strait and Dixon Entrance
March to May only, for Dixon Entrance
questions.explanation: RAMN: issued from March 20 to Remembrance Day in Queen Charlotte Strait, Johnstone Strait, Strait of Georgia, Howe Sound, Haro Strait and Juan de Fuca Strait.

questions.stem: Which warnings can cover offshore marine areas?
options: Strong wind warnings only, in summer
questions.explanation: Strong wind warnings are not issued offshore; gale, storm and hurricane force can cover all marine areas with a forecast.

questions.stem: At what ice build-up rate does ECCC warn of freezing spray?
options: Any ice at all on deck
questions.explanation: Moderate is 0.7 to 2 cm/h and severe is above 2 cm/h.

questions.stem: About how cold must the air be for sea spray to freeze?
options: Below 0 C only, for fresh water
questions.explanation: Salt water needs about minus 2 C; fresh water freezes below 0 C.

questions.stem: What is the difference between a squall watch and a squall warning?
options: A watch means squalls are possible; a warning means expected or occurring
A watch is only for gusts over 60 knots
A warning is issued a day ahead only
questions.explanation: Localized watches give advance notice of possible conditions later in the day.

questions.stem: Where does a warning appear in a regular forecast?
options: Right after the area name, before the forecast, as 'in effect'
At the very end of the forecast text
questions.explanation: The guide places warnings and watches after the zone name, before the forecast text.

questions.stem: What map colour is used for a warning, a watch and an advisory?
questions.explanation: Red warning, yellow watch, grey advisory.

questions.stem: What extra information do BC wind warnings give about the wind?
options: The tide height at the time
Whether it comes with an outflow or an inflow
questions.explanation: UBC notes that wind warnings state whether they are associated with outflows or inflows.
The guide says ice warnings are issued by the Canadian Ice Service.
